# Gūthakhādakapetavatthu (Pv 43)

**ID:** Pv 43
**Section:** Petavatthu (pv)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Gūthakhādakapetavatthu
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Excrement Eating Male Ghost
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pv43

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gūthakhādakapetavatthu* (Pv 43, also referenced as IV.8) is a verse narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection concerning the severe karmic consequences of associating with bad monastics [SuttaCentral; Silk 1994]. The narrative centers on a hungry ghost (*peta*) condemned to reside in a cesspool and consume excrement; in his past human life, he had been a householder who, at the instigation of a corrupt resident monk (*āvāsika*), reviled visiting monks [Silk 1994]. Aside from the gender of the central protagonist, the story is virtually identical to the text that immediately follows it, the *Gūthakhādakapetivatthu* (Pv 44) [Silk 1994; DharmaNexus].

Scholars have noted thematic and narrative parallels in Northern Buddhist literature: Léon Feer pointed to cognate accounts in the Pali Jātaka 41, the Sanskrit *Avadānaśataka*, and Chinese narratives including the *Aśokāvadāna* tradition, where an unrighteous monastic or his associate faces similar foul punishments for insulting the saṅgha [Silk 1994]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus identifies substantial shared material (§0.1–9.1) with Pv 44, extensive citations in the commentary (*Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*), and formulaic overlaps with *Saṭṭhikūṭapetavatthu* (Pv 51) and *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31) [DharmaNexus]. Automated cross-language reuse matches are also recorded between this text and Tibetan Canonical literature as well as the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
